currentContext.expansion: 3i Infotech is an asset-light IT services business - the BRSR reports zero plants in India and internationally - so 'expansion' is stated as capability, partnership and geographic footprint build-out rather than physical capacity. The central expansion programme is the Centre of Excellence (CoE) framework, which was launched across all three business lines in December 2025 and which management expects to be fully operational by the end of Q2 FY 2026-27; the CoEs are intended to combine specialised expertise, reusable frameworks and delivery excellence so the Company can pursue larger and more complex mandates across Cloud and AAA, Infrastructure, BPS, NuRe Intelligence, Information Security and ERP. Alongside this sits partnership-led expansion: in April 2026, through 3i Infotech Inc., the Company entered the SAP Partner Ecosystem, strengthening its ability to deliver SAP Cloud ERP implementation, application management and managed services across SAP S/4HANA Cloud, RISE with SAP and SAP Business Technology Platform, which together with hyperscaler alliances and strategic partnerships across AI, IoT and cybersecurity is stated to expand the addressable market. The NuRe(TM) platform ecosystem - purpose-built solutions across higher education, testing and automation, governance risk and compliance, and AI-powered intelligence - is described as the IP layer of the business and continues to be expanded. Geographically, North America remains the largest and most strategic market (the United States alone contributed 49% of total revenue in FY 2025-26, growing 19% year-on-year) and is to be strengthened through deeper industry focus, expansion of the SAP partnership and enhanced hyperscaler collaboration; India contributed 40% of total revenue with the year's decline attributed to deliberate portfolio rationalisation and a disciplined exit from engagements that did not meet profitability thresholds; the Middle East has been designated a strategic growth market under newly created dedicated regional leadership. New-geography expansion is explicitly at the evaluation stage only: the Company is 'evaluating expansion opportunities in Canada' leveraging its adjacency to the North American business, 'while exploring select countries in East Africa' where digital-infrastructure and public-sector technology investment is accelerating. Management states that across all markets the expansion strategy remains disciplined and focused on delivery readiness, client relevance and sustainable profitability. On the rupee quantum, the accounts state that capital expenditure contracted for at the end of the reporting period is Nil, and the BRSR records 0% of both R&D and capex investment as directed at technologies improving environmental and social impacts (0% in FY 2024-25 as well).

risks.risk: Client concentration - dependence on a limited number of key clients
risks.note: The MD&A risk register carries 'Dependence on Key Clients Risk' explicitly: dependence on a limited number of key clients may affect revenue stability and increase concentration risk. The scale is disclosed elsewhere in the same report - the top 20 clients accounted for 50.6% of FY 2025-26 revenue against a base of 300+ active global clients and 80+ new client wins. Management's stated mitigation is client diversification, stronger retention, long-term contracts and a healthy pipeline. This is structural because the CEO's own diagnosis of the FY 2025-26 revenue shortfall was that it was 'not a delivery challenge but a new business acquisition challenge' - i.e. the concentration is being addressed by a sales engine that management concedes is still being rebuilt.

risks.risk: Geographic concentration in the US and MENA, with live geopolitical exposure
risks.note: The Geopolitical Risk row quantifies the exposure directly: targeted mitigations were implemented in FY 2025-26 for MENA exposure (~10%) amid geopolitical disruption - strengthened business continuity protocols, workload diversification and engagement monitoring - while US revenue (~40%) is described as only 'partially insulated' through annuity-led managed services. (The Corporate Overview separately puts the US at 49% / 49.4% of FY 2025-26 revenue, so the two disclosures of US share disagree; both are recorded as stated.) Country risk is described as including asset expropriation, trade restrictions and currency devaluation, with outsourcing to foreign countries adding exposure amid host-nation policy change. Mitigation is local expert consultants per country, regular assessment, and diversification via expansion in India and APAC.

risks.risk: Cybersecurity and data privacy - a risk that has already crystallised
risks.note: Cybersecurity and Data Privacy are separate rows of both the MD&A risk register and the BRSR material-issues table, citing weak access controls, unsecured communication tools, third-party vulnerabilities, data breaches, regulatory penalties and loss of client trust. This is not hypothetical: on May 16, 2026 (FY 2026-27) the Company identified a potential cyber security incident involving a suspected ransomware attack on its IT infrastructure and network, engaged an independent forensic firm, and intimated CERT-In, SEBI and the Stock Exchanges; the MD&A adds that it activated its cyber incident response framework with a CERT-In-empanelled forensic auditor and implemented containment, forensic investigation and recovery (sentence truncated). Management states the incident has not impacted business continuity and there is no material impact on overall operations. Mitigations listed are VAPT, RBAC, Bluetooth/USB restrictions, controlled external email, disabled Wi-Fi on company mobile devices, secure email gateway, encryption and multi-factor authentication.

risks.risk: Legacy regulatory, tax and legal exposures requiring ongoing management attention
risks.note: The MD&A groups these under Regulatory & Compliance and Financial & Legal Risks: legacy regulatory matters may require ongoing management attention due to historical process gaps, documentation limitations and evolving compliance expectations; legacy tax matters, contractual disputes and ongoing litigations may create financial and operational uncertainty; and adverse outcomes in material disputes or claims could impact profitability, liquidity, cash flows and stakeholder confidence. Read against the rest of the report this maps to the unresolved FEMA non-compliances from 2005-2022 (with APR filing compliance on hold for years after 2019), the forensic audit and High-Powered Committee process, and the complaints filed with the Economic Offences Wing and SEBI in February 2026. The Company states it continues to pursue resolution of legacy exposures through appropriate legal, regulatory and settlement mechanisms.

risks.risk: Talent attrition, skill gaps and key-person dependency
risks.note: Two distinct rows - 'Key and Senior Management Risk' and 'People and Talent Risk' - flag that unexpected leadership exits may disrupt operations, execution and regulatory compliance, amplified by SEBI's LODR mandate to fill such roles within three months with penalties for non-compliance, and that talent shortages, attrition and skill gaps may impact productivity, service delivery and competitiveness. The MD&A's own Potential Threats list adds that dependence on key leadership personnel and specialised talent may create continuity risks. The magnitude is disclosed elsewhere in the report: 26.9% voluntary attrition and a 43.6% permanent-employee turnover rate in FY 2025-26 (up from 32.7% in FY 2024-25), with the Board's Report conceding attrition and retention are a challenge 'more so for the Company'. Mitigation is succession planning, a centralised talent repository, market-aligned compensation, premium job portals and referrals, Coursera/Udemy upskilling, a revamped ESOP policy and a revived Management Trainee programme.

risks.risk: Cautious, selective enterprise technology spending and macroeconomic uncertainty
risks.note: Macroeconomic uncertainty, inflationary pressures and geopolitical developments may continue to influence enterprise technology spending and investment priorities; clients are exercising greater caution in approving transformation programmes with increased emphasis on measurable ROI, business outcomes and near-term value realisation; and technology spending remains active but selective, directed towards productivity enhancement, automation, cybersecurity and cost optimisation. This is the demand-side risk that already showed up in FY 2025-26 - the CEO notes revenue growth remained below internal expectations amid cost pressures and prolonged decision-making cycles.

risks.risk: Outsourcing/data-privacy regulation and vendor-governance practices that can end contracts independent of performance
risks.note: Changes in outsourcing regulations, data privacy and operational risk frameworks may affect business models and engagement structures, particularly in regulated sectors - material given BFSI is 36.5% of revenue. The sharper structural point is the next line: vendor governance requirements, contract reviews and vendor rotation policies in certain industries may influence contract continuity IRRESPECTIVE of service delivery performance, i.e. revenue can be lost for reasons entirely outside the Company's delivery control. The BRSR adds regulatory non-compliance in certain jurisdictions can bring penalties, reputational damage and potential criminal consequences; mitigation is a global compliance monitoring system, external consulting firms and regularly updated Compliance Obligation Registers.

risks.risk: Capital structure and profitability constraining near-term shareholder distributions
risks.note: Listed in the MD&A's Potential Threats: current profitability levels and the Company's capital structure may limit flexibility with respect to near-term shareholder distributions. This is corroborated by the Board's decision not to recommend any dividend for FY 2025-26 despite reporting a profit, and by the fact that the Company raised Rs 64.10 Crores through a rights issue during the year of which Rs 8.25 Crores remained unutilised at March 31, 2026 with the deployment deadline deferred to September 30, 2026. Related structural rows are Competition and Market Saturation Risk (pricing pressure, reduced market share, limited growth as most customers are already served), Deal and Project Review Risk (inaccurate proposals, pricing or profitability assessments), SLA Non-Compliance Risk (delivery delays and financial penalties), Third-party Contracting Risk and Intellectual Property Infringement Risk.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: 3i Infotech Limited provides IT consulting services and software solutions to customers across multiple industry verticals, delivered through three lines of business - Applications, Automation and Analytics (AAA); Infrastructure Services (IS); and Business Process Services (BPS). The Company serves a diverse global customer base, primarily enterprises in Banking, Financial Services and Insurance (BFSI), along with healthcare, manufacturing, E-commerce, education, telecom, media & entertainment, energy and government sectors. It operates through offices in India and a branch in Sharjah, UAE, with additional international presence held through subsidiaries, and had 300+ active global clients and 3,700+ total employees in FY 2025-26.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The IT services industry is shifting from traditional transformation programmes to outcome-driven, platform-led and AI-enabled engagements; demand is expected to be supported by application modernisation, hybrid cloud adoption, cyber resilience, enterprise automation and human-AI collaboration.
- AAA services are expected to benefit from increasing investments in application modernisation and AI-led transformation initiatives.
- Infrastructure Services are well positioned to capitalise on growing demand for data centre modernisation, cloud adoption, and management of hybrid and multi-cloud environments.
- Business Process Services are likely to gain from continued enterprise focus on cost optimisation, operational efficiency and process automation, particularly across BFSI, healthcare and other regulated sectors.
- The AI/ML Centre of Excellence is positioned as the innovation engine as AI becomes integral to pre-sales, delivery and platform innovation.
- India: technology services landscape expected to benefit from continued expansion of Global Capability Centres (GCCs), increasing cloud migration, sustained investment in digital public infrastructure and deeper AI integration into enterprise platforms and workflows; India IT services market cited at US$ 42.7 bn in 2025 growing to US$ 78.1 bn by 2034 (6.9% CAGR 2026-2034, IMARC).
- North America: valued at US$ 3,026.3 bn in 2025 (32.1% of the global IT market), projected 6.1% CAGR through 2030, supported by AI-driven IT automation, cloud transformation, cybersecurity and next-generation digital infrastructure.
- APAC: valued at US$ 3,035.9 bn in 2025 (32.2% of the global IT market), projected ~9.3% CAGR through 2030, outpacing most other regions; Forrester projects regional tech spending +9.3% in 2026; IDC expects APAC AI/GenAI spending to reach US$ 370 bn by 2029.
- Middle East: valued at US$ 307.2 bn in 2025, projected ~13.9% CAGR through 2030, one of the fastest-growing technology markets globally, driven by GCC government-led transformation (Saudi Vision 2030, UAE digital agenda, Egypt's New Administrative Capital), hyperscale data centres in Riyadh and Abu Dhabi, and an expanding fintech ecosystem.
- Cloud is evolving from a storage/scalability platform to a foundational layer for AI-driven enterprises, with hybrid and multi-cloud architectures reducing reliance on a single provider.
- Blockchain emerging as trusted infrastructure via smart contracts, tokenisation and cryptographic verification across banking, supply chains, real estate and capital markets.
- Counter-drivers management flags: macroeconomic uncertainty, spending scrutiny, talent availability, cybersecurity risks and evolving regulatory requirements may influence client decision-making; ongoing Middle East geopolitical tensions create near-term uncertainty for the region's technology outlook and elevate the importance of business continuity planning and diversified delivery infrastructure.
- Demand environment experienced during FY 2025-26: across key markets organisations remained cautious in technology investments, navigating cost pressures, prolonged decision-making cycles and geopolitical uncertainties.
- Margin/quality levers cited: operational discipline, strengthened cost governance, improved delivery efficiency, a sharper focus on higher-quality scalable revenue, and a more disciplined revenue mix.
- Working-capital lever: Days Sales Outstanding improved from 65 days in FY 2024-25 to 57 days in FY 2025-26.
- Balance-sheet position cited as a platform for growth: a debt-free balance sheet; the Company has not availed any credit facility and is therefore not required to obtain a credit rating.
- Human resources: talent pipeline described as healthy, but attrition and retention remain a challenge for the industry and 'more so for the Company'.
- No order book or order-inflow figure is disclosed in the routed text. Management refers qualitatively to pipeline only: 'go-to-market investments that are beginning to translate into a stronger pipeline and business opportunities' (FY 2026-27 entry position).
- 'a stronger pipeline focus across geographies and businesses' cited as one of the corrective actions on new business acquisition; 'We have started seeing some initial gains from these changes and will see more results in the coming years.'

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Vision 2030 (released last year): triple the FY 2024-25 revenue base by FY 2029-30; the ambition is stated to remain 'firmly intact' despite headwinds during FY 2025-26.
- FY 2026-27 marks the beginning of the growth and scaling phase of Vision 2030, entered with a strengthened sales organisation, a fully operational Centre of Excellence framework, strategic OEM partnerships and go-to-market investments.
- Portfolio anchored on three core service lines - Application, Automation and Analytics (AAA), Infrastructure Services (IS) and Business Process Services (BPS) - complemented by product-led offerings under the NuRe(TM) ecosystem delivering industry-specific platforms and IP-driven solutions.
- Horizontally integrate an AI-led services capability across all portfolios, infusing intelligence and automation into every service line (sentence truncated mid-word in the routed text).
- Fix the identified new-business-acquisition gap (management explicitly states revenue shortfall was not a delivery challenge) via Centre of Excellence creation, senior and mid-level leadership additions across sales, pre-sales and delivery, sales process and operations improvements, and a stronger pipeline focus across geographies and businesses.
- Deliberately streamline low-margin engagements, revitalise the sales organisation and address legacy matters to improve revenue mix quality and long-term competitiveness.
- Maintain capital discipline as a governing priority: all capital investments undergo comprehensive review covering market opportunity, business case, risk assessment and expected return on investment, with a Products Innovation Sub-Committee evaluating product development initiatives and the evolution roadmap.
- Invest selectively in opportunities that strengthen long-term capabilities while maintaining financial discipline.
- Strengthen client engagement, delivery resilience and geographical diversification, and diversify into Healthcare, Retail, Manufacturing and Government verticals to offset US geopolitical/policy/macro uncertainty.
- Continue strengthening the internal governance architecture - Standard Operating Procedures formalised across organisational functions and proactive risk control metrics embedded across financial and operational departments.
- Resolve legacy matters through the Sub-Committee on Legacy Matters (subsidiary loan restructuring and FEMA non-compliances from 2005-2022), acting on High-Powered Committee recommendations verifying the FY 2024-25 forensic audit findings, and engaging the RBI directly.
- Continue to focus on and build human potential to improve operating parameters in the coming years.
- The routed governance and entity-structure text contains NO stated dividend policy, payout philosophy, buyback intent or reinvestment doctrine - those statements sit in the Board's Report and Chairman's message routed to other domains, and an honest gap is recorded here rather than an inferred philosophy. What the governance chapters do establish is the OVERSIGHT architecture around capital: the Board reviews at its meetings key matters including operations and financial results, the annual operating plan, statutory- and internal-auditor observations, compliance with applicable laws and pending taxation and litigation matters; the Group Chief Executive Officer apprises the Board at each meeting on Company performance; and an action-taken report on decisions is tabled at the immediately succeeding meeting. The one explicit capital-related proposal in this material is share-based: Special Business item 3 of the 33rd AGM notice seeks members' approval, on the recommendation of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee and the Board, to modify the Employee Stock Option Plan 2023 - replacing the existing 30%/30%/40% three-year vesting schedule with a four-year schedule vesting 25% each year, and revising the performance-linked vesting matrix so that employees rated '3' also become eligible for 100% vesting (ratings 5 and 4 already at 100%, rating 2 at 50%, rating 1 no vesting, all unchanged). Board-composition governance is stated as compliant: six directors as on March 31, 2026 (four Independent including one Independent Woman Director, two Non-Executive), conformity with Regulation 17, no director on more than 10 board-level committees or chairing more than 5, none an Independent Director in more than 7 listed companies, none of the Directors or KMP related inter-se, declarations of independence received from all Independent Directors, no Independent Director resigned before expiry of tenure during FY 2025-26, all Independent Directors registered in the IICA databank, six Board meetings held during FY 2025-26 (May 14, July 31, August 13, September 17 and November 12, 2025 and February 13, 2026) all within the 120-day maximum gap and with requisite quorum, and a separate meeting of Independent Directors held on February 13, 2026. The BRSR Section A general-disclosure table states Paid-up Capital of Rs 2,07,40,37,670 (recorded here as an identity disclosure, not lifted from the balance sheet).
- EXPLICIT ABSENCE OF ESG TARGETS - the single most important ESG disclosure here: BRSR Section B item 5 states 'Although we have not established specific commitments, goals, or timelines for all policies we have put in place mechanisms to track key performance indicators', listing only Customer Net Promoter Score (NPS), shareholder complaints, employee satisfaction surveys, and resource consumption surveys covering water, paper and electricity. Item 6, performance against specific commitments/goals/targets, is answered 'Not Applicable'. There is therefore no dated, quantified ESG target of any kind in this annual report.
- Certifications mapped to the NGRBC principles (BRSR Section B item 4), listed against Principle 1 and Principle 2: ISO 9001:2015, ISO 20000:2018, ISO 27001:2022 and CMMi Level 5.
- NGRBC policy architecture is complete on paper but unevenly ratified: policies cover all nine principles (P1-P9 all 'Yes'), but Board approval is recorded as 'Yes' for only P1, P4, P5, P6 and P8 and 'No' for P2, P3, P7 and P9; the policies are translated into procedures for all principles except P2 and P7; and they extend to value-chain partners for all except P2. Policy web link: https://www.3i-infotech.com/investors/
- Four ESG items are classified as OPPORTUNITIES with positive financial implications rather than risks in the BRSR material-issues table: Diversity (fostering an inclusive workplace culture and ensuring underrepresented communities have equitable access to upskilling); Responsible AI (staying ahead of automation and AI transformation for sustained relevance); Community development (eradicating illiteracy including IT illiteracy through education, empowering rural populations, health education and healthcare provision); and Corporate Governance & Business Ethics (creating a culture of integrity, transparency and accountability). Eleven other material issues are classified as risks with negative financial implications.
- Human-capital ESG actions actually taken during FY 2025-26 (from the risk-mitigation columns, so these are stated actions rather than aspirations): the ESOP policy was revamped to recognise and reward high performers with emphasis on leadership development; the Management Trainee programme was revived/revitalised to build a sustainable talent pipeline; investments were made in learning platforms including Coursera and Udemy; compensation structures were aligned with market benchmarks; and hiring channels were strengthened through premium job portals, referral programmes and internal job postings. A structured succession plan supported by a centralised talent repository has been developed.
- Grievance redressal: mechanisms are in place ('Yes') for Customers and Value Chain Partners, both reporting 0 complaints filed and 0 pending with 'Nil' remarks in FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25. Published grievance policy links exist for Investors and Shareholders (https://www.3i-infotech.com/investors/) and for Customers and Value Chain Partners (https://www.3i-infotech.com/grievance-redressal/); the Employees and workers policy sits on the internal Knowledge Management Portal only; and the web link for the Communities grievance policy is stated as 'Not Available'.
- Workplace safety and equality disclosures are all stated nil or affirmative: zero sexual-harassment complaints on every line of the POSH disclosure (0 pending at April 1, 2025; 0 received in FY 2025-26; 0 pending beyond 90 days; 0 disposed of; 0 pending at March 31, 2026), an Internal Complaints Committee constituted, the policy covering all permanent, contractual, temporary and trainee employees, and affirmed compliance with the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961.
- CSR is a stated non-obligation for the year: the provisions of Section 135 were not applicable to the Company for FY 2025-26 as it did not meet the prescribed thresholds, and it was therefore not required to spend any amount on CSR activities - although a CSR Committee is constituted and a Board-approved CSR Policy is published on the website.
- Cyber resilience is being positioned as an ESG/governance capability rather than only a control: subsequent to year-end, in early FY 2026-27, the Company activated its established cyber incident response framework following a cybersecurity event, working with an external CERT-In-empanelled forensic auditor and implementing comprehensive containment, forensic investigation and recovery (the sentence is truncated in the routed text).
- Risk-management governance: a comprehensive Risk Management Framework is established to identify, assess, mitigate, monitor and manage risks; the Board's Risk Management Committee provides oversight and reviews the evolving risk landscape; the Audit Committee has additional oversight of financial risks and controls; an independent internal audit function conducts periodic reviews with findings presented to the Audit Committee; and the framework is aligned with regulatory requirements and industry best practice and reviewed periodically.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: 3i Infotech is an asset-light IT services business - the BRSR reports zero plants in India and internationally - so 'expansion' is stated as capability, partnership and geographic footprint build-out rather than physical capacity. The central expansion programme is the Centre of Excellence (CoE) framework, which was launched across all three business lines in December 2025 and which management expects to be fully operational by the end of Q2 FY 2026-27; the CoEs are intended to combine specialised expertise, reusable frameworks and delivery excellence so the Company can pursue larger and more complex mandates across Cloud and AAA, Infrastructure, BPS, NuRe Intelligence, Information Security and ERP. Alongside this sits partnership-led expansion: in April 2026, through 3i Infotech Inc., the Company entered the SAP Partner Ecosystem, strengthening its ability to deliver SAP Cloud ERP implementation, application management and managed services across SAP S/4HANA Cloud, RISE with SAP and SAP Business Technology Platform, which together with hyperscaler alliances and strategic partnerships across AI, IoT and cybersecurity is stated to expand the addressable market. The NuRe(TM) platform ecosystem - purpose-built solutions across higher education, testing and automation, governance risk and compliance, and AI-powered intelligence - is described as the IP layer of the business and continues to be expanded. Geographically, North America remains the largest and most strategic market (the United States alone contributed 49% of total revenue in FY 2025-26, growing 19% year-on-year) and is to be strengthened through deeper industry focus, expansion of the SAP partnership and enhanced hyperscaler collaboration; India contributed 40% of total revenue with the year's decline attributed to deliberate portfolio rationalisation and a disciplined exit from engagements that did not meet profitability thresholds; the Middle East has been designated a strategic growth market under newly created dedicated regional leadership. New-geography expansion is explicitly at the evaluation stage only: the Company is 'evaluating expansion opportunities in Canada' leveraging its adjacency to the North American business, 'while exploring select countries in East Africa' where digital-infrastructure and public-sector technology investment is accelerating. Management states that across all markets the expansion strategy remains disciplined and focused on delivery readiness, client relevance and sustainable profitability. On the rupee quantum, the accounts state that capital expenditure contracted for at the end of the reporting period is Nil, and the BRSR records 0% of both R&D and capex investment as directed at technologies improving environmental and social impacts (0% in FY 2024-25 as well).

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Centre of Excellence (CoE)-led operating model advanced during FY 2025-26 to deepen domain expertise and drive greater solution consistency
- AI/ML Centre of Excellence described as the Company's innovation engine, bringing together consulting expertise, reusable accelerators and domain capabilities across applications, infrastructure and business processes
- NuRe(TM) platform ecosystem expanded during the year, supporting platform-led delivery and differentiation
- Broad global client base - 300+ active global clients, 80+ new client wins in FY 2025-26, 5+ countries served
- Three complementary lines of business (AAA, IS, BPS) allowing the Company to address application modernisation, hybrid-cloud/infrastructure and process-automation demand from the same client base
- Diversified delivery footprint across the US, India, MEA and APAC, with geographical diversification and diversification into Healthcare, Retail, Manufacturing and Government cited by the Chairman as the response to external uncertainty
- Annual Report recognised for the third consecutive year at the LACP Vision Awards 2024-25, scoring 98 out of 100 and ranking 35th globally, plus a Technical Achievement Award

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Client concentration - dependence on a limited number of key clients — The MD&A risk register carries 'Dependence on Key Clients Risk' explicitly: dependence on a limited number of key clients may affect revenue stability and increase concentration risk. The scale is disclosed elsewhere in the same report - the top 20 clients accounted for 50.6% of FY 2025-26 revenue against a base of 300+ active global clients and 80+ new client wins. Management's stated mitigation is client diversification, stronger retention, long-term contracts and a healthy pipeline. This is structural because the CEO's own diagnosis of the FY 2025-26 revenue shortfall was that it was 'not a delivery challenge but a new business acquisition challenge' - i.e. the concentration is being addressed by a sales engine that management concedes is still being rebuilt.
- Geographic concentration in the US and MENA, with live geopolitical exposure — The Geopolitical Risk row quantifies the exposure directly: targeted mitigations were implemented in FY 2025-26 for MENA exposure (~10%) amid geopolitical disruption - strengthened business continuity protocols, workload diversification and engagement monitoring - while US revenue (~40%) is described as only 'partially insulated' through annuity-led managed services. (The Corporate Overview separately puts the US at 49% / 49.4% of FY 2025-26 revenue, so the two disclosures of US share disagree; both are recorded as stated.) Country risk is described as including asset expropriation, trade restrictions and currency devaluation, with outsourcing to foreign countries adding exposure amid host-nation policy change. Mitigation is local expert consultants per country, regular assessment, and diversification via expansion in India and APAC.
- Cybersecurity and data privacy - a risk that has already crystallised — Cybersecurity and Data Privacy are separate rows of both the MD&A risk register and the BRSR material-issues table, citing weak access controls, unsecured communication tools, third-party vulnerabilities, data breaches, regulatory penalties and loss of client trust. This is not hypothetical: on May 16, 2026 (FY 2026-27) the Company identified a potential cyber security incident involving a suspected ransomware attack on its IT infrastructure and network, engaged an independent forensic firm, and intimated CERT-In, SEBI and the Stock Exchanges; the MD&A adds that it activated its cyber incident response framework with a CERT-In-empanelled forensic auditor and implemented containment, forensic investigation and recovery (sentence truncated). Management states the incident has not impacted business continuity and there is no material impact on overall operations. Mitigations listed are VAPT, RBAC, Bluetooth/USB restrictions, controlled external email, disabled Wi-Fi on company mobile devices, secure email gateway, encryption and multi-factor authentication.
- Legacy regulatory, tax and legal exposures requiring ongoing management attention — The MD&A groups these under Regulatory & Compliance and Financial & Legal Risks: legacy regulatory matters may require ongoing management attention due to historical process gaps, documentation limitations and evolving compliance expectations; legacy tax matters, contractual disputes and ongoing litigations may create financial and operational uncertainty; and adverse outcomes in material disputes or claims could impact profitability, liquidity, cash flows and stakeholder confidence. Read against the rest of the report this maps to the unresolved FEMA non-compliances from 2005-2022 (with APR filing compliance on hold for years after 2019), the forensic audit and High-Powered Committee process, and the complaints filed with the Economic Offences Wing and SEBI in February 2026. The Company states it continues to pursue resolution of legacy exposures through appropriate legal, regulatory and settlement mechanisms.
- Talent attrition, skill gaps and key-person dependency — Two distinct rows - 'Key and Senior Management Risk' and 'People and Talent Risk' - flag that unexpected leadership exits may disrupt operations, execution and regulatory compliance, amplified by SEBI's LODR mandate to fill such roles within three months with penalties for non-compliance, and that talent shortages, attrition and skill gaps may impact productivity, service delivery and competitiveness. The MD&A's own Potential Threats list adds that dependence on key leadership personnel and specialised talent may create continuity risks. The magnitude is disclosed elsewhere in the report: 26.9% voluntary attrition and a 43.6% permanent-employee turnover rate in FY 2025-26 (up from 32.7% in FY 2024-25), with the Board's Report conceding attrition and retention are a challenge 'more so for the Company'. Mitigation is succession planning, a centralised talent repository, market-aligned compensation, premium job portals and referrals, Coursera/Udemy upskilling, a revamped ESOP policy and a revived Management Trainee programme.
- Cautious, selective enterprise technology spending and macroeconomic uncertainty — Macroeconomic uncertainty, inflationary pressures and geopolitical developments may continue to influence enterprise technology spending and investment priorities; clients are exercising greater caution in approving transformation programmes with increased emphasis on measurable ROI, business outcomes and near-term value realisation; and technology spending remains active but selective, directed towards productivity enhancement, automation, cybersecurity and cost optimisation. This is the demand-side risk that already showed up in FY 2025-26 - the CEO notes revenue growth remained below internal expectations amid cost pressures and prolonged decision-making cycles.
- Outsourcing/data-privacy regulation and vendor-governance practices that can end contracts independent of performance — Changes in outsourcing regulations, data privacy and operational risk frameworks may affect business models and engagement structures, particularly in regulated sectors - material given BFSI is 36.5% of revenue. The sharper structural point is the next line: vendor governance requirements, contract reviews and vendor rotation policies in certain industries may influence contract continuity IRRESPECTIVE of service delivery performance, i.e. revenue can be lost for reasons entirely outside the Company's delivery control. The BRSR adds regulatory non-compliance in certain jurisdictions can bring penalties, reputational damage and potential criminal consequences; mitigation is a global compliance monitoring system, external consulting firms and regularly updated Compliance Obligation Registers.
- Capital structure and profitability constraining near-term shareholder distributions — Listed in the MD&A's Potential Threats: current profitability levels and the Company's capital structure may limit flexibility with respect to near-term shareholder distributions. This is corroborated by the Board's decision not to recommend any dividend for FY 2025-26 despite reporting a profit, and by the fact that the Company raised Rs 64.10 Crores through a rights issue during the year of which Rs 8.25 Crores remained unutilised at March 31, 2026 with the deployment deadline deferred to September 30, 2026. Related structural rows are Competition and Market Saturation Risk (pricing pressure, reduced market share, limited growth as most customers are already served), Deal and Project Review Risk (inaccurate proposals, pricing or profitability assessments), SLA Non-Compliance Risk (delivery delays and financial penalties), Third-party Contracting Risk and Intellectual Property Infringement Risk.
